text.//colourCodes: ioquake3 and iortcw take only letters and digits after the escape; a caret before anything else is shown.

protocolOptions.//infoRules: iortcw sets g_needpass but never puts it in the status; its engine gives it only in getinfo, as RTCW's own browser reads it.

password.//maxLength: Info_SetValueForKey refuses 64 characters or more, so a longer password would never reach the server.
password.//refusedCharacters: kpded2 rebuilds "set password %s", so a space splits the value; iortcw cuts the command line at every '+' and ends a token at "//" or "/*"; both refuse '"', '\' and ';' in userinfo, and Quake 2 expands '$'.
